blocks.why: Normal nights off — keep the usual bed and wake times so the month starts with no debt.
Same again; steady rhythm is the cheapest fatigue protection you'll get all month.
Hold the anchor sleep — the first block of flying starts with three early reports.
Full night before an afternoon standby, so a callout at 14:00 local finds you rested.
Standby released at 20:00 local; straight to a normal night and start pulling the clock earlier.
Standby opens 06:00 local, so lights out by 20:30 local to get seven clear hours before an 03:45 alarm.
In bed by 19:30 local after standby — the 85-minute commute means a 03:30 alarm for a 05:40 local report.
Short one on the sofa after the ARN turn to take the edge off before another early tomorrow.
Second early in a row — bank the full eight hours before the 04:00 local alarm.
Top-up nap; tomorrow is an 11-hour four-sector day off a 05:40 local report.
Earliest realistic bedtime — the third consecutive early start is the one that bites.
First late report of the block; sleep in and pay back three mornings of accumulated debt.
Long night before a 12-hour duty that doesn't finish until after midnight.
Hour down before leaving home — the last sector lands 23:51 local and you'll be awake past 01:00.
Home about 01:45 local; get straight to bed but set an alarm so the evening sleep will come.
Split day — back to bed at 19:30 local to be usable for a 05:05 local report.
Recovery night after the early four-sector day, and the base load for a duty ending 02:10 local.
Prophylactic nap before a 12h55 duty whose last landing is right in the middle of the WOCL.
Home around 03:35 local; sleep now but keep it to six and a half hours so tonight still works.
Hard turnaround of the body clock — 19:00 local bedtime is the only way to face a 05:45 local departure.
Nap after the ARN turn; tomorrow is a four-sector Dublin day off the same early report.
Second consecutive 02:55 local alarm — protect the eight hours, no evening plans.
Long recovery night; tomorrow reports at midday and finishes near midnight.
Bank an hour before an 11h21 duty landing at 23:11 local.
Straight to bed on the day off after a 01:00 local arrival home.
The day off is really a clock-reset day — early night for another 05:45 local departure.
Ten hours if you can get them; the next three duties all run into or through the night.
Nap before report — CDG doesn't land back until 00:03 local and you're flying again tomorrow afternoon.
Only sleep opportunity between two back-to-back night finishes; guard it, curtains shut, phone off.
Non-negotiable nap — tonight's last sector departs CDG at 02:15 local and lands 03:05 local, straight through the low point.
Home about 04:30 local after the worst duty of the month; sleep it off in the morning.
Second sleep on the day off to clear the deficit before another duty ending at 02:24 local.
Hour down before the double Barcelona; you'll be at the controls at 01:00 local body time.
Home around 03:50 local — sleep long, four days off start now.
Re-anchor to a normal night straight away rather than drifting through the days off.
Normal night off, holding the pattern.
Start walking bedtime earlier — the last duty of the month reports at 04:35 local.
Half hour in the afternoon so the very early bedtime doesn't have to do all the work.
Lights out 19:00 local — a 05:15 local departure means leaving home at 03:10.
Nap on arriving home after the Frankfurt turn to close out the month cleanly.
Back onto a normal night to finish the roster period in credit.

conflicts.statement: Three consecutive early reports (04:40Z, 05:10Z, 04:40Z on 08–10 Sep) each need a 03:30 local alarm because of the 85-minute LHR commute; evening sleep onset rarely comes early enough to cover this, so you arrive at the 11h01 four-sector day on 10 Sep with two nights of accumulated debt.
options: Protect a genuine 19:30 local bedtime on 8 and 9 Sep — no social commitments, no late meals
Take the afternoon naps on 8 and 9 Sep as planned rather than treating them as optional
Consider crashpad or airport hotel on the nights of 7 and 9 Sep to convert 85 minutes of commute into sleep
Flag the 10 Sep duty to crewing as the one at risk and be ready to use commander's discretion in the other direction

conflicts.statement: Duty on 12 Sep ends 23:21Z (00:21 local 13 Sep), the single day off is 13 Sep, and 14 Sep reports at 04:05Z (05:05 local) — the 'day off' is entirely consumed swinging the body clock backwards by roughly nine hours in one step.
options: Use the split sleep in the plan: short morning sleep on 13 Sep, alarm at 08:45 local, then a second sleep from 19:30 local
Get outdoor daylight late morning on 13 Sep and avoid bright light after 18:00 local
Ask crewing whether 14 Sep can be swapped to a later report given the preceding night finish
Accept the 14 Sep duty will be flown on about seven hours of fragmented sleep and plan controlled rest in the cruise with the captain

conflicts.statement: Same pattern, harder: 15 Sep finishes 01:10Z on 16 Sep (02:10 local), one day off, then 17 Sep reports 04:05Z (05:05 local). You land in the middle of the WOCL and are due back at report 27 hours later.
options: Cap the morning sleep on 16 Sep at about six and a half hours so a 19:00 local bedtime is achievable
No caffeine after midday on 16 Sep
Request removal of either 15 Sep or 17 Sep — this pairing is the second-worst in the month
Treat 17 and 18 Sep as a two-day early block and clear the evenings of both

conflicts.statement: 17 and 18 Sep are back-to-back 04:05Z reports (05:45 local departures), the second being a 9h16 four-sector Dublin day, with only a 17h17 rest that yields roughly 14h at home once the commute is taken out.
options: Nap on arriving home on 17 Sep as planned, then a 19:00 local bedtime
Pre-pack and pre-fuel the car the night before to buy 20 minutes of sleep
Stay near base on the night of 17/18 Sep
Brief the captain on 18 Sep that fatigue risk peaks on the third and fourth sectors

conflicts.statement: Third occurrence of the backward swing: 19 Sep ends 22:41Z (23:41 local), one day off on 20 Sep, then 21 Sep reports 04:05Z (05:05 local) for a 10h42 four-sector duty.
options: Sleep on arrival on 20 Sep, be up by 09:30 local, then early night
Bright light and exercise on the morning of 20 Sep to pull the clock forward
Ask for 21 Sep to be moved later — this is the third identical pattern in eight days and the cumulative effect is what matters

conflicts.statement: 22 Sep ends 23:33Z (00:33 local 23 Sep) and 23 Sep reports 14:25Z (15:25 local) — about 14h50 of rest, but only around 12 hours at home after two 85-minute commutes, and that single sleep has to carry you through a duty finishing at 03:05 local on 24 Sep.
options: Treat the 23 Sep pre-duty nap as part of the rest, not a bonus — set an alarm for it
Ask crewing to break the 22/23 Sep pairing; two consecutive WOCL-crossing finishes with one short rest between them is the worst feature of this roster
Consider a hotel near LHR on the night of 22/23 Sep to recover the commute time as sleep
Plan in-seat controlled rest on the 23 Sep CDG sectors and agree the rotation with the captain before departure

conflicts.statement: The 23 Sep duty operates AT797 CDG–LHR departing 00:15Z and landing 01:35Z, with off-duty at 02:05Z — an approach and landing flown squarely inside the 02:00–06:00 local window of lowest alertness, at the end of an 11h40 duty.
options: Nap before report on 23 Sep and take controlled rest on the ARN sectors
Save caffeine for the CDG turnaround rather than using it early in the duty
Do not drive home unaided after this duty — arrange a lift, taxi, or airport hotel
File a fatigue report if the landing feels degraded; it is the datapoint that changes future rosters

conflicts.statement: 25 Sep repeats the pattern: AT369 departs BCN 22:49Z and lands LHR 00:54Z with off-duty 01:24Z, so a fourth sector is flown at 01:00–02:00 body time at the end of an 11h44 duty.
options: Take the 25 Sep pre-duty nap without fail
Split the drive home or stay at the airport if you feel impaired
Four days off follow — protect the morning sleep on 26 Sep and re-anchor to a normal night the same evening

conflicts.statement: The final duty reports at 03:35Z (04:35 local) for a 05:15 local departure, meaning a 02:25 local alarm, coming immediately after four days off during which the body clock will have drifted later.
options: Walk bedtime 30–45 minutes earlier on each of 27, 28 and 29 Sep rather than shifting in one jump
Take the short afternoon nap on 29 Sep so the 19:00 local bedtime isn't carrying all the load
Avoid alcohol and screens on the evening of 29 Sep
Consider an airport hotel for the night of 29/30 Sep to convert commute into sleep

conflicts.statement: The two standby days (5 and 7 Sep) print only an 'Off Duty' time and a duty length, with no start time; I have read them as windows ending at the stated time — 14:00–20:00 local on 5 Sep and 06:00–14:00 local on 7 Sep — and applied no reporting offset, as the roster's 40-minute offset is stated as 'before STD'.
options: Confirm the standby window start times with crewing before relying on the 7 Sep 06:00 local reading
If 7 Sep standby actually starts later, the 6 Sep early bedtime can be relaxed by the same amount
Assume home standby with the 85-minute commute inside any callout notice period; if it is airport standby, the plan needs a further 85 minutes of margin
